summary: Richard Salomon works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics, having studied under Ludo Rocher. He was a visiting researcher at Soka University in 2007 and served as a professor at the University of Washington (attested 1998-2017; emeritus attested 2026).

Richard Schmidt was an Indologist who completed his doctorate under Richard Pischel and Karl Friedrich Geldner (~1886-1890) and habilitation (-1898) at Halle-Wittenberg. He served as Privatdozent at Halle-Wittenberg (~1898-1909) and ordinary professor at the University of Münster (1910).
Richard Shilleto was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He was educated at Repton School, Shrewsbury School (~1823-1828), and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1828-1832).

Richard Sproat works in computational linguistics. He studied at UC San Diego (1977-1981) and MIT (1981-1985), later holding posts at the University of Illinois (2003-2009), Oregon Health and Science University (2009-2012), and Google (2012).

Richard Sylvan was a philosopher who studied at Victoria University of Wellington (~1954-1958) and Princeton University (~1959-1963). He held posts at the University of Sydney (~1963-1966) and the Australian National University as a fellow (1971).

Richard W. Lariviere is an Indologist who studied at the University of Iowa and the University of Pennsylvania under Ludo Rocher. He held administrative posts at UT Austin, the University of Kansas, the University of Oregon, and the Field Museum.

Richard Wilhelm was a Sinologist who studied at the Eberhard-Ludwigs-Gymnasium and the University of Tübingen (~1891-1895). He served as a guest professor at Peking University (1923) and held the Sinology chair at Goethe University Frankfurt (1924).

Richard von Garbe was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth and Königsberg. He held posts at the University of Königsberg (1878-1880, 1894) and served as chairholder at Tübingen (1895-1927).

Richard von Glahn is a scholar of Sinology and history/archaeology. He served as a professor at the University of California, Los Angeles (~1987) and as a visiting fellow at the University of Tokyo (1988-1989).
Rigdzin Shikpo was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under teachers Chögyam Trungpa and Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche.

Riika J. Virtanen is a scholar in Tibetology. She completed her doctoral studies at the University of Helsinki under supervisors Asko Parpola, Klaus Karttunen, and Hannu Riikonen, and also studied under Sangye Tandar Naga.
Rikizan Ishikawa was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (~1962-1971). He later served as Professor of Buddhist Studies at Komazawa University from ~1989 to 1997.

Ringu Tulku is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at the Namgyal Institute, CIHTS, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University. A student of Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, he has taught at Naropa University.

Rinzin Thargyal is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He completed his Magister degree at the University of Oslo (-1985), where he studied under supervisors Fredrik Barth and Arne Martin Klausen.

Rita Langer is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who earned her PhD at the University of Hamburg and studied at SOAS and the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies. She has held posts at the University of Bristol.

Rita M. Gross was a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at UW-Milwaukee and the University of Chicago. She held posts at UW-Madison (~1977-1979) and UW-Eau Claire (~1979-1998), and taught at Mindrolling Lotus Garden (~2003-2015).

Ritu Birla is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at Columbia University (~1991-1996). She has held a post as Professor Emerita in the Department of History at the University of Toronto (~2003).

Rizong Sras Rinpoche was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who underwent monastic training at Drepung Loseling Monastery (1950-1959). He served as Abbot of Gyume Tantric College (~1975-1984), Drepung Loseling Monastery (1984), and Samstanling Monastery.

Rob Linrothe is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and history/archaeology who earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (~1984-1992). He held posts at Skidmore College (1992-2009) and Northwestern University (2010-2022).

Rob Nairn was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Zimbabwe, King's College London, and University of Edinburgh. He held posts in law and criminology at the University of Zimbabwe (~1966-1976) and University of Cape Town (~1976-1981).
